analysis.title: Reiterating EssilorLuxottica Buy rec, PT 240
key_insights: UBS Specialist Sales reiterates Buy on EssilorLuxottica with a PT of EUR 240. UBS values the core business at EUR 220, growing at more than 6%, and says the market assigns little to zero value to smart glasses.

Positioning is neutral and governance concerns remain an issue. UBS says Meta/EL keeps a first-mover advantage, wearables penetration and mix keep improving, and competitive fears are ahead of the evidence.

Bloomberg reports a Czech billionaire (Strnad) offered EUR 30B for Delfin Sarl at a 30% discount to net asset value, in an Oct. 20 letter valid for 30 days. All eight Delfin shareholders would have to approve changes to ownership restrictions.
Delfin shareholder Leonardo Maria Del Vecchio said he knew of the offer and would keep Delfin's ownership Italian. Delfin declined to comment.

Privacy/regulation: UBS sees the EDPB statement on smart glasses as pointing to regulation through dialogue, not prohibition. UBS puts the probability of an outright ban in Europe as very low. The shares trade at about a 30% discount to the core business's standalone value.

UBS estimates a global smart glasses market of about EUR 90bn by 2040 even with subdued European adoption. Excluding Europe entirely (about 4% of OSG in EMEA), UBS still sees high single-digit organic growth.
Q3 26 results: group sales EUR 7,486m, +2% vs consensus. Constant-FX growth was +7.2% (consensus +6.2%, UBSe +6.5%). The core business grew more than 6% cFX and wearables about 20%.
Q3 by channel at cFX: Professional Solutions +3.4% (cons +2.4%, UBSe +2.5%) and Direct to Consumer +10.6% (cons +9.6%, UBSe +10.0%).
Q3 by region at cFX: North America +4.7% (cons +3.8%, UBSe +5.5%), EMEA +7.5% (cons +6.3%, UBSe +6.0%), APAC +15.7% (cons +14.1%, UBSe +12.0%), LatAm +7.1% (cons +8.0%, UBSe +5.6%).

Conference call: no slowdown in the core, with consistent growth in the first week of Q4. Transitions-lens penetration in smart glasses reached about 60% in own retail, and prescription penetration about 33%. More than 90% of Nuance sales include prescription lenses.

Management says protests in Italy and France had no material impact. FX helped Q3 and could remain a tailwind in Q4. Management will give a fuller wearables update at year end or in February. No geographic sales split was disclosed.

Guidance is unchanged: solid total revenue growth and broadly aligned adjusted operating profit growth over the next five years at constant exchange rates. EssilorLuxottica disclosed wearables revenue separately for the first time.

UBS says Delfin's risks look overstated. Leonardo Maria Del Vecchio, a Delfin heir, has called the stake a 'crown jewel'. Insiders bought more than EUR 20m over the past month. Delfin has other options, including a listing like EXOR, selling other financial assets, or higher dividends.

UBS Evidence Lab surveys: design remains the most important purchase factor (about 93% of owners, about 92% of non-owners), ahead of AI functionality. Purchase intention for smart glasses was about 61% in the second survey vs about 57% in September.

Ahead of Q3, UBS expected FY27 revenue growth of about +8.6% but adjusted EBIT (cFX) broadly flat vs FY26e. It cited gross margin headwinds from the growing smart glasses mix and the absence of tariff refund benefits.

market_movers.rationale: UBS Specialist Sales reiterates Buy on EssilorLuxottica. It values the core business at EUR 220 and says the market gives little or no value to smart glasses. EssilorLuxottica's US ADR is not confirmed in the report, so the ticker is left blank.

sector_views.sector: Consumer Staples & Luxury (eyewear and smart glasses)
sector_views.rationale: UBS sees EssilorLuxottica's core growth above 6%, an underpriced wearables business and an attractive risk/reward despite a tougher consumer backdrop.

earnings_insights: EssilorLuxottica Q3 26 (reported 10/20): group sales EUR 7,486m, +2% vs consensus and in line with UBSe. cFX growth +7.2% (consensus +6.2%, UBSe +6.5%), core business above 6% cFX, wearables about +20%.
Q3 26 reported channel growth at cFX: Professional Solutions +3.4% (cons +2.4%, UBSe +2.5%), Direct to Consumer +10.6% (cons +9.6%, UBSe +10.0%).

Q3 26 reported regional growth at cFX: North America +4.7% (cons +3.8%, UBSe +5.5%), EMEA +7.5% (cons +6.3%, UBSe +6.0%), APAC +15.7% (cons +14.1%, UBSe +12.0%), LatAm +7.1% (cons +8.0%, UBSe +5.6%). UBS says the beat was across the board except LatAm.
UBS estimates (forecasts): FY27 revenue growth +8.6%, adjusted EBIT (cFX) broadly flat vs FY26e. UBSe EBIT is about 3% ahead of consensus.
Valuation (UBS estimates): 17.6x 2027e and 15.7x 2028e P/E, with 2027e-30e sales and EPS CAGRs of +8% and +12%. The PT is EUR 244 in the Q3 review (previously EUR 247), reflecting peer de-rating.

trade_ideas.description: Buy EssilorLuxottica, PT EUR 240 (UBS Specialist Sales reiteration of the UBS Research Buy rating)
trade_ideas.rationale: The core business is valued at EUR 220 and grows at more than 6%, while the market assigns little to zero value to smart glasses.
trade_ideas.risk: Governance concerns around Delfin, smart glasses competition and European privacy regulation.

risk_factors: Governance and succession uncertainty at Delfin (about 32% stake), including the Czech billionaire's EUR 30B offer and possible stake transfers among heirs.
Competition in smart glasses, including Google's launch and a possible Apple launch in late 2027.
European privacy regulation of smart glasses, including the EDPB statement and local restrictions.
A tougher Q4 comparison base and a weaker consumer backdrop.
FY27 gross margin pressure from smart glasses mix, no tariff refund benefit and raw material prices.
vol_and_positioning: UBS describes positioning in EssilorLuxottica as neutral.
geopolitical: Protests in Italy and France had no material impact on EssilorLuxottica, per management. Some stores were temporarily closed and damaged.
